problem: VLMaps-style open-vocabulary maps fuse all noisy, viewpoint-dependent CLIP evidence into a single representation with little treatment of uncertainty, so they are unstable over long horizons and struggle to balance adaptability with robustness on mobile rovers.
motivation: Rovers in unstructured or planetary settings face partial observability, sensor noise, changing lighting and objects that appear or disappear. The map has to stay stable yet adapt to new evidence, which calls for explicit confidence modeling and separate short-term and long-term memory.
key_idea: Fuse tile-level multi-scale CLIP embeddings into a top-down grid using geometric, semantic and temporal confidence, and promote only confident, coherent, multi-view-supported cells from a short-term memory into a persistent long-term landmark memory.
insight: The paper gives no quantitative ablation, only qualitative heatmaps. In the 'hammer' query example the STM is noisy while the LTM is sparser and more reliable, which suggests the promotion gate (confidence, coherence, viewpoint diversity) filters noise. Weighting heatmaps by coherence keeps consistent regions visible even at low confidence.
method: Tile-level multi-scale CLIP: each RGB frame is split into coarse and fine tiles encoded by CLIP ViT-L/14 (OpenAI weights), trading spatial precision for throughput and robustness to motion.
Spatial projection: sampled depth points are back-projected with the SLAM pose into the global frame, given fused coarse+fine tile embeddings, and accumulated in a top-down grid map.

Confidence-aware STM fusion: point/cell confidence combines geometric (distance decay, multi-view), semantic (cosine agreement with cell embedding, soft gating) and temporal (decay) cues; cell update S<-S+c_i e_i, W<-lambda W + c_i, e_C=S/||S||.

STM-to-LTM promotion: a cell is promoted if accumulated confidence W>tau_c, coherence (norm of mean of normalized embeddings) >tau_h, and viewpoint diversity (bitmask of angle bins) is satisfied; a new high-confidence observation can overwrite a contradicting LTM cell.
Language querying: CLIP text embedding is compared to cell embeddings by cosine similarity; heatmap H = similarity*coherence; top-1 navigation target ranking uses raw cell confidence.
ROS 2 implementation: modular node on a Waveshare UGV Jetson Orin rover with RTAB-Map localization, publishing embeddings, confidence grids and heatmaps to RViz.

setting.action_space: none implemented; produces semantic heatmaps and top-1 navigation target cells

numbers_note: Workshop paper with only a qualitative proof-of-concept demonstration (heatmap figures); no quantitative results or benchmarks reported.
results: Qualitative only: real-time operation on a Jetson Orin rover with natural-language queries such as 'plant' and 'hammer'. The STM heatmap is noisy while the LTM is sparser and more reliable. No baselines or metrics are given.
limitations: No quantitative evaluation, ablations or baseline comparison (e.g., against VLMaps or DualMap); navigation itself is not evaluated.
Tile-level CLIP embeddings lose spatial precision compared to pixel-wise or segmentation-based features; the authors plan to add SAM.
Computation is offloaded to an external computer rather than running fully onboard, and the hand-set thresholds and decay parameters are not analyzed.
